claim: The asymmetric summation of kinetically distinct glutamate inputs across the dendrites of retinal 'starburst' amacrine cells is one of the several mechanisms that have been proposed to underlie their direction-selective properties.
source: The asymmetric summation of kinetically distinct glutamate inputs across the dendrites of retinal 'starburst' amacrine cells is one of the several mechanisms that have been proposed to underlie their direction-selective properties, but experimentally verifying input kinetics has been a challenge.
evidence: This claim is supported by references to existing literature proposing this mechanism.

claim: Experimentally verifying input kinetics in starburst amacrine cells has been a challenge.
source: The asymmetric summation of kinetically distinct glutamate inputs across the dendrites of retinal 'starburst' amacrine cells is one of the several mechanisms that have been proposed to underlie their direction-selective properties, but experimentally verifying input kinetics has been a challenge.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field prior to this study.

claim: Signals measured from proximal dendrites were relatively sustained compared to those measured from distal dendrites.
source: We found that signals measured from proximal dendrites were relatively sustained compared to those measured from distal dendrites.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Differences in signal kinetics between proximal and distal dendrites were observed across a range of stimulus sizes.
source: These differences were observed across a range of stimulus sizes and appeared to be shaped mainly by excitatory rather than inhibitory network interactions.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing consistent differences across multiple stimulus conditions.

claim: Kinetic differences between proximal and distal inputs appeared to be shaped mainly by excitatory rather than inhibitory network interactions.
source: These differences were observed across a range of stimulus sizes and appeared to be shaped mainly by excitatory rather than inhibitory network interactions.
evidence: This is supported by pharmacological experiments blocking inhibitory pathways.

claim: The steady-state vesicle release rate was approximately 3 times larger at proximal sites compared to distal sites.
source: Temporal deconvolution analysis suggests that the steady-state vesicle release rate was ~3 times larger at proximal sites compared to distal sites.
evidence: This is derived from temporal deconvolution analysis of experimental data.

claim: Input kinetics play an important role in shaping direction selectivity at low stimulus velocities.
source: Using a connectomics-inspired computational model, we demonstrate that input kinetics play an important role in shaping direction selectivity at low stimulus velocities.
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling based on experimental data.

claim: The results provide direct support for the 'space-time wiring' model for direction selectivity.
source: Taken together, these results provide direct support for the 'space-time wiring' model for direction selectivity.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the experimental and modeling results.

claim: The radiating dendrites of retinal GABAergic/cholinergic 'starburst' amacrine cells are the first points in the visual system to exhibit direction selectivity.
source: The radiating dendrites of retinal GABAergic/cholinergic 'starburst' amacrine cells (starbursts) are the first points in the visual system to exhibit direction selectivity (Euler et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Euler et al., 2002.

claim: Object motion away from the soma generates large calcium responses in distal starburst dendrites.
source: Object motion away from the soma generates large calcium responses in distal starburst dendrites, from where they release GABA and acetylcholine (ACh).
evidence: This is established knowledge about starburst cell function.

claim: Motion toward the soma evokes weak responses in starburst dendrites.
source: By contrast, motion toward the soma evokes weak responses.
evidence: This is established knowledge about starburst cell function.

claim: Starbursts play a critical role in shaping direction-selective responses of downstream ganglion cells.
source: Starbursts play a critical role in shaping direction-selective (DS) responses of downstream ganglion cells (DSGCs), and thus, understanding how they compute direction is of principal interest.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: No single mechanism alone may be critically required for direction selectivity in starburst dendrites.
source: Decades of intense investigations have identified several mechanisms that underlie direction selectivity in starburst dendrites, although no single mechanism alone may be critically required (Ding et al., 2016; Hausselt et al., 2007; Kim et al., 2014; Hanson et al., 2019; reviewed by Murphy-Baum et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: The 'space-time wiring' model for direction selectivity relies on the kinetic properties of distinct sources of glutamatergic input.
source: A model that has garnered recent attention relies on the kinetic properties of distinct sources of glutamatergic input, which is referred to as the 'space-time wiring' model for direction selectivity (Greene et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Greene et al., 2016 and Kim et al., 2014.

claim: The proximal and distal dendritic regions of ON and OFF type starburst amacrine cells receive synaptic inputs from anatomically distinct types of glutamatergic bipolar cells.
source: The space-time wiring model for direction selectivity is inspired by connectomic analysis in the mouse retina showing that the proximal and distal dendritic regions of ON and OFF type starburst amacrine cells receive synaptic inputs from anatomically distinct types of glutamatergic bipolar cells (BCs) (Greene et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by connectomic analysis cited from Greene et al., 2016 and Kim et al., 2014.

claim: The axon terminals of bipolar cells contacting starburst dendrites stratify at distinct depths within the inner plexiform layer.
source: As the axon terminals of these BCs stratify at distinct depths within the inner plexiform layer (IPL; Ding et al., 2016; Greene et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2014)—and in general BC axonal stratification patterns are linked to their kinetic properties (Awatramani and Slaughter, 2000; Baden et al., 2016; Franke et al., 2017; Gaynes et al., 2022; Strauss et al., 2022)—it has been hypothesized that different types of BCs contacting proximal and distal starburst dendrites have distinct response kinetics (Greene et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ding et al., 2016; Greene et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2014.

claim: BC axonal stratification patterns are linked to their kinetic properties.
source: As the axon terminals of these BCs stratify at distinct depths within the inner plexiform layer (IPL; Ding et al., 2016; Greene et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2014)—and in general BC axonal stratification patterns are linked to their kinetic properties (Awatramani and Slaughter, 2000; Baden et al., 2016; Franke et al., 2017; Gaynes et al., 2022; Strauss et al., 2022)—it has been hypothesized that different types of BCs contacting proximal and distal starburst dendrites have distinct response kinetics (Greene et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Proximal inputs near the starburst soma are predicted to be mediated by BC types that support tonic patterns of glutamate release.
source: Specifically, it is predicted that proximal inputs near the starburst soma are mediated by BC types that support tonic patterns of glutamate release, while distal inputs are mediated by BC types that release their vesicles more transiently.
evidence: This is a prediction from the space-time wiring model.

claim: Distal inputs are predicted to be mediated by BC types that release their vesicles more transiently.
source: Specifically, it is predicted that proximal inputs near the starburst soma are mediated by BC types that support tonic patterns of glutamate release, while distal inputs are mediated by BC types that release their vesicles more transiently.
evidence: This is a prediction from the space-time wiring model.

claim: The arrangement of sustained proximal and transient distal inputs would result in optimal input summation along starburst dendrites during centrifugal motion.
source: This arrangement would result in an optimal input summation along starburst dendrites during centrifugal (soma-to-dendrite) motion, as experimentally noted.
evidence: This is an inference from the model and experimental observations.

claim: The space-time wiring model for direction selectivity is algorithmically similar to classic correlation-type motion detectors described in rodents and primates.
source: The space-time wiring model for direction selectivity is algorithmically similar to classic correlation-type motion detectors described elsewhere in the visual system in both rodents and primates (Lien and Scanziani, 2018; De Valois and Cottaris, 1998), as well as the fly optic lobe (Haag et al., 2016; Leong et al., 2016; Behnia et al., 2014), and thus appears to reflect a core computational principle.
evidence: This is supported by citations to work in other systems.

claim: The space-time wiring model appears to reflect a core computational principle.
source: The space-time wiring model for direction selectivity is algorithmically similar to classic correlation-type motion detectors described elsewhere in the visual system in both rodents and primates (Lien and Scanziani, 2018; De Valois and Cottaris, 1998), as well as the fly optic lobe (Haag et al., 2016; Leong et al., 2016; Behnia et al., 2014), and thus appears to reflect a core computational principle.
evidence: This is an inference based on similarities across species.

claim: There is scant evidence that the kinetics of glutamatergic input varies along the length of starburst dendrites.
source: While it is an attractive model for direction selectivity, there is scant evidence that the kinetics of glutamatergic input varies along the length of starburst dendrites.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of evidence prior to this study.

claim: BC5s (including types 5i, o, and t) and BC7 make 'ribbon' synapses predominantly on the distal and proximal dendrites of ON starbursts, respectively.
source: Direct electrophysiological measurements revealed that BC5s (including types 5i, o, and t) and BC7, which make 'ribbon' synapses predominantly on the distal and proximal dendrites of ON starbursts, respectively, have similar temporal properties (Ichinose et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ichinose et al., 2014.

claim: BC5s and BC7 have similar temporal properties according to direct electrophysiological measurements.
source: Direct electrophysiological measurements revealed that BC5s (including types 5i, o, and t) and BC7, which make 'ribbon' synapses predominantly on the distal and proximal dendrites of ON starbursts, respectively, have similar temporal properties (Ichinose et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ichinose et al., 2014.

claim: Regional differences in input kinetics were noted when BC output was measured postsynaptically using voltage-clamp techniques.
source: Regional differences in input kinetics were noted when BC output was measured postsynaptically using voltage-clamp techniques (Fransen and Borghuis, 2017; but see Stincic et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Fransen and Borghuis, 2017.

claim: Electrophysiological recordings do not provide precise information regarding the anatomical location of synaptic inputs.
source: However, these electrophysiological recordings do not provide precise information regarding the anatomical location of synaptic inputs.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of electrophysiological methods.

claim: Genetically encoded fluorescent glutamate sensors (iGluSnFRs) have provided an alternate way to measure BC output kinetics.
source: To this end, genetically encoded fluorescent glutamate sensors (iGluSnFRs) have provided an alternate way to measure BC output kinetics (Borghuis et al., 2013; Marvin et al., 2013; Yonehara et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Borghuis et al., 2013; Marvin et al., 2013; Yonehara et al., 2013.

claim: Most BCs of the same polarity (including the BC5s and BC7 types) have similar temporal properties to spatially restricted stimuli.
source: However, recent imaging studies have found that most BCs of the same polarity (including the BC5s and BC7 types) have similar temporal properties, at least to spatially restricted stimuli that are relevant to local starburst dendritic computations (Franke et al., 2017; Strauss et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Franke et al., 2017 and Strauss et al., 2022.

claim: Direction selectivity remains intact under conditions in which all BC input to starbursts is pharmacologically blocked and the starburst network is directly stimulated in relative isolation.
source: Finally, optogenetic studies have demonstrated that direction selectivity remains intact under conditions in which all BC input to starbursts is pharmacologically blocked and the starburst network is directly stimulated in relative isolation (Hanson et al., 2019; Sethuramanujam et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hanson et al., 2019 and Sethuramanujam et al., 2016.

claim: Previous results provide little support for the space-time wiring model for direction selectivity.
source: Taken together, previous results provide little support for the space-time wiring model for direction selectivity.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the state of evidence prior to this study.

claim: Spots of light (200 μm in diameter) centered on the imaging field evoked robust iGluSnFR signals throughout the first ~60–80 μm section of starburst dendrites.
source: Spots of light (200 μm in diameter) centered on the imaging field evoked robust iGluSnFR signals throughout the first ~60–80 μm section of starburst dendrites, where glutamatergic BCs are known to make synapses (Ding et al., 2016; Greene et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experiments.

claim: Glutamatergic BCs are known to make synapses in the first ~60–80 μm section of starburst dendrites.
source: Spots of light (200 μm in diameter) centered on the imaging field evoked robust iGluSnFR signals throughout the first ~60–80 μm section of starburst dendrites, where glutamatergic BCs are known to make synapses (Ding et al., 2016; Greene et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ding et al., 2016 and Greene et al., 2016.

claim: The peak amplitudes of the iGluSnFR signals measured over small regions of interest were relatively stable across the length of single starburst dendrites.
source: The peak amplitudes of the iGluSnFR signals measured over small regions of interest (ROIs; 5×5 μm2) were relatively stable across the length of single starburst dendrites (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The magnitude of the sustained phase significantly decreased as a function of distance from the soma.
source: However, the magnitude of the sustained phase significantly decreased as a function of distance (Figure 1C; ΔF/F=0.80±0.29 at proximal sites; ΔF/F=0.29±0.16 at distal sites, measured in 20 dendrites in 4 retinas from 4 mice; *p<0.001, t-test).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The sustained/transient index (STi) systematically decreased with distance from the soma.
source: As a result, the sustained/transient index (STi) computed from the plateau/peak ratio, systematically decreased with distance from the soma (Figure 1D; STi=0.33±0.06 for proximal, 0.16±0.05 for distal ROIs; *p<0.001, t-test)
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: STi=0 indicates a purely transient response with no plateau phase.
source: (Note, STi=0 indicates a purely transient response with no plateau phase, and STi=1 indicates a purely sustained response where peak and plateau phases are equal).
evidence: This is a definition of the STi metric used in the study.

claim: STi=1 indicates a purely sustained response where peak and plateau phases are equal.
source: (Note, STi=0 indicates a purely transient response with no plateau phase, and STi=1 indicates a purely sustained response where peak and plateau phases are equal).
evidence: This is a definition of the STi metric used in the study.

claim: STis were significantly lower in imaging planes that captured distal dendrites compared to those that captured proximal dendritic responses.
source: We found that STis were significantly lower in imaging planes that captured distal dendrites (STi=0.21±0.07; μ±s.d.); compared to those that captured proximal dendritic responses (STi=0.34±0.07; μ±s.d.) (n=242 proximal ROIs; n=563 distal ROIs; 8 retinas from 8 mice; 10 FOVs; *p<0.001, t-test; Figure 2A–C)
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: The STi for individual ROIs measured across the population was independent of response amplitude.
source: The STi for individual ROIs measured across the population was independent of response amplitude, indicating that the estimated differences in signal kinetics are not strongly compromised by signal-to-noise and/or sensor saturation issues (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The latencies and rise times for responses measured at proximal and distal sites were similar.
source: In addition, we also found that the latencies and rise times for responses measured at proximal and distal sites were similar (Figure 2D and E)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: Small differences in axonal path lengths between proximal and distal BCs do not result in significant transmission delays.
source: In addition, we also found that the latencies and rise times for responses measured at proximal and distal sites were similar (Figure 2D and E), indicating that the small differences in axonal path lengths between proximal and distal BCs do not result in significant transmission delays, as previously envisioned (Kim et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference from the latency and rise time data.

claim: Inputs to proximal starburst dendrites originate mainly from BC7s.
source: Anatomical studies show that inputs to proximal starburst dendrites originate mainly from BC7s, while inputs to distal dendrites arise from BC5s (including types BC5i, o, and t; Greene et al., 2016; Ding et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by citations to anatomical studies.

claim: Inputs to distal starburst dendrites arise from BC5s (including types BC5i, o, and t).
source: Anatomical studies show that inputs to proximal starburst dendrites originate mainly from BC7s, while inputs to distal dendrites arise from BC5s (including types BC5i, o, and t; Greene et al., 2016; Ding et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by citations to anatomical studies.

claim: The kinetic differences of iGluSnFR responses may reflect the properties of distinct BC types.
source: Anatomical studies show that inputs to proximal starburst dendrites originate mainly from BC7s, while inputs to distal dendrites arise from BC5s (including types BC5i, o, and t; Greene et al., 2016; Ding et al., 2016), indicating that the kinetic differences of iGluSnFR responses may reflect the properties of distinct BC types.
evidence: This is an inference based on anatomical data and the observed kinetic differences.

claim: iGluSnFR responses at BC7 terminals were sustained, regardless of their peak amplitude.
source: We found that iGluSnFR responses at BC7 terminals were sustained, regardless of their peak amplitude (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The most appreciable changes in iGluSnFR fluorescence occurred at the axon terminals of BC7s.
source: The most appreciable changes in iGluSnFR fluorescence occurred at the axon terminals, suggesting that the sensor signals reflect the vesicle release dynamics of individual BC7s (James et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experiments.

claim: The sensor signals reflect the vesicle release dynamics of individual BC7s.
source: The most appreciable changes in iGluSnFR fluorescence occurred at the axon terminals, suggesting that the sensor signals reflect the vesicle release dynamics of individual BC7s (James et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an inference supported by citation to James et al., 2019.

claim: BC7s are the source of sustained proximal input.
source: While these results lend support to the idea that BC7s are the source of sustained proximal input, we were unable to express the sensor in BC5s and could not directly confirm that these were the sources of transient signals observed in distal starburst dendrites.
evidence: This is supported by the sustained responses observed at BC7 terminals.

claim: The authors were unable to express the sensor in BC5s.
source: While these results lend support to the idea that BC7s are the source of sustained proximal input, we were unable to express the sensor in BC5s and could not directly confirm that these were the sources of transient signals observed in distal starburst dendrites.
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of the experimental approach.

claim: When white-noise stimuli were used, the authors failed to observe significant kinetic differences in proximal and distal iGluSnFR responses.
source: When white-noise stimuli were used to characterize the temporal properties of BCs using reverse-correlation techniques, we failed to observe significant kinetic differences in proximal and distal iGluSnFR responses.
evidence: This is a direct observation from experiments using white-noise stimuli.

claim: The input impulse responses were biphasic for both proximal and distal inputs.
source: We found the input impulse responses were biphasic for both proximal and distal inputs (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The probability of glutamate release from BC terminals appears to be transiently depressed following a burst of vesicle release during continuous stimulus regimes.
source: Thus, the probability of glutamate release from BC terminals appears to be transiently depressed, following a burst of vesicle release, during continuous stimulus regimes.
evidence: This is an inference from the biphasic impulse responses.

claim: Similar biphasic kernels have been observed in recent imaging studies.
source: Similar biphasic kernels have been observed in recent imaging studies (Franke et al., 2017; Strauss et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Franke et al., 2017 and Strauss et al., 2022.

claim: Under conditions where the circuit is continually stimulated at high frequencies, input kinetics are unlikely to play a role in shaping direction selectivity in starburst dendrites.
source: As the biphasic nature of the distal—but not proximal—input is critical to the success of models generating direction selectivity (Kim et al., 2014; Fransen and Borghuis, 2017), we conclude that under conditions where the circuit is continually stimulated at high frequencies, input kinetics are unlikely to play a role in shaping direction selectivity in starburst dendrites.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the white-noise stimulus results.

claim: Increasing the spot diameter systematically decreased the peak amplitude of BC responses, indicative of the recruitment of the inhibitory surround.
source: Next, to investigate whether cell-intrinsic or network mechanisms shape BC kinetics, we examined how iGluSnFR responses were affected by stimulus size. Increasing the spot diameter systematically decreased the peak amplitude of BC responses, indicative of the recruitment of the inhibitory surround (Figure 4A; Franke et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A and citation to Franke et al., 2017.

claim: The distinction in the kinetics of proximal and distal inputs remained clear across stimulus sizes, although they were generally more pronounced for stimuli that were >200 μm.
source: Importantly, the distinction in the kinetics of proximal and distal inputs remained clear across stimulus sizes, although they were generally more pronounced for stimuli that were >200 μm (Figure 4B–E, control; n=71 proximal and 431 distal ROIs, 5 FOVs, 4 retinas from 4 mice; *p<0.001, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4B-E.

claim: The application of a cocktail of antagonists containing both GABA and ionotropic glutamate receptor antagonists augmented responses, especially those evoked by larger spots.
source: Indeed, the application of a cocktail of antagonists containing both GABA and ionotropic glutamate receptor antagonists (5 µM gabazine and 100 µM TPMPA, 20 µM CNQX, respectively)—which blocks inhibitory inputs from amacrine and horizontal cells—augmented responses, especially those evoked by larger spots (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The kinetics of the iGluSnFR responses at proximal and distal ROIs remained distinct even in the presence of synaptic blockers.
source: These effects reduced the overall STi as compared to control, but the kinetics of the iGluSnFR responses at proximal and distal ROIs remained distinct (Figure 4B–E, drug cocktail; n=71 proximal and 431 distal ROIs, 5 FOVs, 4 retinas from 4 mice; *p<0.001, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4B-E.

claim: Inhibitory networks modulate BC responses but do not appear to account for the sustained/transient differences observed.
source: Thus, while the inhibitory networks modulate BC responses, they do not appear to account for the sustained/transient differences observed here.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pharmacological experiments.

claim: Blocking glutamate/GABA receptor-mediated pathways revealed a spread of lateral excitation.
source: Blocking glutamate/GABA receptor-mediated pathways using the drug cocktail also revealed a somewhat unexpected spread of lateral excitation.
evidence: This is an observation from the pharmacological experiments.

claim: Under inhibitory receptor blockade, the light-evoked iGluSnFR responses continued to grow even when the spots sizes were increased significantly beyond the size of BC dendritic fields.
source: Under inhibitory receptor blockade, the light-evoked iGluSnFR responses continued to grow even when the spots sizes were increased significantly beyond the size of BC dendritic fields (~50 µm; Figure 4A, n=71 proximal and 431 distal ROIs, 5 FOVs, 4 retinas from 4 mice; *p<0.01).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The maximal peak response was evoked for spots that were ~200 µm diameter.
source: The maximal peak response was evoked for spots that were ~200 µm diameter.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experiments.

claim: The amplitude of the plateau phase was further increased by ~23% in the proximal and ~20% in the distal dendritic sites, between 200 µm and 800 µm spot sizes.
source: Interestingly, the amplitude of the plateau phase was further increased by ~23% in the proximal and ~20% in the distal dendritic sites, between 200 µm and 800 µm (*p<0.01, t-test).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data and statistical analysis.

claim: Lateral excitation is likely to be attributed to electrical coupling, which occurs between BCs as well as amacrine cells.
source: Such lateral excitation is likely to be attributed to electrical coupling, which occurs between BCs as well as amacrine cells (Sigulinsky et al., 2020; Arai et al., 2010; Asari and Meister, 2014).
evidence: This is an inference supported by citations to previous work on electrical coupling.

claim: The kinetic diversity of BC responses is maintained in the absence of inhibition, suggesting that they are shaped in large part by excitatory network mechanisms.
source: The finding that the kinetic diversity of BC responses is maintained in the absence of inhibition, suggests that they are shaped in large part by excitatory network mechanisms.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pharmacological experiments.

claim: Time-varying vesicle release rates from proximal and distal BCs were estimated by deconvolving the iGluSnFR response with an idealized quantal response described by an alpha function with decay kinetics ~30 ms.
source: Time-varying vesicle release rates from proximal and distal BCs were estimated by deconvolving the iGluSnFR response with an idealized quantal response described by an alpha function with decay kinetics ~30 ms (Figure 5B, inset), which was obtained by matching the kinetics of 'spontaneous' quantal responses (Figure 5A).
evidence: This describes the deconvolution method used to estimate release rates.

claim: Convolving the average quantal response with the inferred trains of vesicle release events produced a signal similar to the original iGluSnFR measurement.
source: Indeed, convolving the average quantal response with the inferred trains of vesicle release events (Figure 5C) produced a signal similar to the original iGluSnFR measurement (Figure 5D).
evidence: This validates the deconvolution approach by showing it can reconstruct the original signal.

claim: Proximal BCs release vesicles throughout the duration of the stimulus.
source: The release profiles of proximal and distal BCs obtained in this manner support the notion that they have different capacities to release vesicles in response to light stimuli: proximal BCs release vesicles throughout the duration of the stimulus, while distal BCs release a large fraction of their vesicles at the onset of the light stimulus (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by the release rate estimates shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Distal BCs release a large fraction of their vesicles at the onset of the light stimulus.
source: The release profiles of proximal and distal BCs obtained in this manner support the notion that they have different capacities to release vesicles in response to light stimuli: proximal BCs release vesicles throughout the duration of the stimulus, while distal BCs release a large fraction of their vesicles at the onset of the light stimulus (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by the release rate estimates shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Starburst dendritic sectors are relatively electrically isolated from each other.
source: Previous experimental and modeling studies have shown starburst dendritic sectors to be relatively electrically isolated from each other (Poleg-Polsky et al., 2018; Morrie and Feller, 2018; Ozaita et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The potential for intra-dendritic signaling in starburst cells is likely to be minimal.
source: Since the potential for intra-dendritic signaling is likely to be minimal, we constructed a simple ball-and-stick model (NEURON), rather than a more complex network model.
evidence: This is an inference based on previous studies showing electrical isolation of dendritic sectors.

claim: Responses measured in the soma rose rapidly in the preferred direction compared to those evoked in the null direction, owing to the asymmetric distribution of inputs.
source: The voltage responses measured from the model cell soma were qualitatively similar to those measured experimentally. For example, responses measured in the soma rose rapidly in the preferred direction compared to those evoked in the null direction, owing to the asymmetric distribution of inputs (Figure 6A, middle panel; Ankri et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a result from the computational model supported by citation to Ankri et al., 2020.

claim: The model accurately recapitulated direction selectivity measured in the distal intracellular Ca2+ signals similar to results from two-photon Ca2+ imaging experiments.
source: The model also accurately recapitulated direction selectivity measured in the distal intracellular Ca2+ signals (Figure 6A, bottom traces) similar to results from two-photon Ca2+ imaging experiments (Euler et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a result from the computational model validated by comparison to experimental data.

claim: Direction selectivity in the model was strongly dependent on stimulus velocity.
source: As expected for a mechanism that relies on a fixed delay, this direction selectivity was strongly dependent on stimulus velocity.
evidence: This is a result from the computational model.

claim: In the model based on experimentally determined input kinetics, anisotropic summation occurs most robustly for slow-moving stimuli (<0.5 mm/s).
source: In our model based on the experimentally determined input kinetics, anisotropic summation occurs most robustly for slow-moving stimuli (<0.5 mm/s).
evidence: This is a result from the computational model.

claim: When the kinetics of proximal and distal BCs were exchanged, the directional preference was reversed from preferring centrifugal to centripetal motion.
source: First, when the kinetics of proximal and distal BCs were exchanged (i.e., proximal BCs were made transient and the distal BCs were made sustained), the directional preference was reversed from preferring centrifugal to centripetal motion (resulting in a negative DSi; Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a result from the computational model shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The strength of the directional preference was stronger for the native compared to the switched BC distributions.
source: Notably, the strength of the directional preference was stronger for the native compared to the switched BC distributions, indicating that the kinetic mechanisms work in concert with intrinsic dendritic mechanisms (Hausselt et al., 2007; Tukker et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a result from the computational model.

claim: DSi was strongly decreased when all BCs were made either sustained or transient.
source: Second, DSi was strongly decreased when all BCs were made either sustained or transient (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a result from the computational model shown in Figure 6B.

claim: BC distribution manipulations had a statistically significant effect on DSi up to 1 mm/s.
source: In all cases, the direction selectivity was most robust for slow-moving stimuli, and we found that these BC distribution manipulations had a statistically significant effect on DSi up to 1 mm/s (p<0.05; one-way analysis of variance, ANOVA; Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the model results shown in Figure 6B.

claim: DSi was significantly higher in the condition when BC distribution followed the native sustained-transient distribution over when all BCs were sustained for velocities up to 0.5 mm/s.
source: DSi was significantly higher in the condition when BC distribution followed the native sustained-transient distribution over when all BCs were sustained (p<0.0005; t-test), for velocities up to 0.5 mm/s.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the model results.

claim: When sustained input was incrementally converted into transient ones, direction selectivity decreased linearly.
source: Third, when we fixed the BC input locations and incrementally converted sustained input into transient ones (starting from the proximal site furthest from the soma), direction selectivity decreased linearly (Figure 6C; velocity 0.15 mm/s).
evidence: This is a result from the computational model shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The amount of asymmetric temporal summation decreases as inputs with weaker plateau phases are swapped in.
source: This is presumably because the amount of asymmetric temporal summation decreases as inputs with weaker plateau phases are swapped in.
evidence: This is an inference from the modeling results.

claim: For velocities with the strongest DS response, there were linear relationships between the magnitude of DSi and the mean distance between the sustained and transient BC input.
source: We found that for velocities with the strongest DS response (positive for the control condition, and negative for the swapped release profile condition), there were indeed linear relationships between the magnitude of DSi and the mean distance between the sustained and transient BC input (R2≈0.208 and 0.269, respectively, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the context of realistic estimates of glutamate input kinetics, the 'space-time' wiring model for direction selectivity holds merit under specific stimulus conditions.
source: Thus, we conclude that in the context of realistic estimates of glutamate input kinetics, the 'space-time' wiring model for direction selectivity holds merit under specific stimulus conditions.
evidence: This is the main conclusion from the modeling results.

claim: Recent models of direction selectivity in the fly visual system and mammalian retina incorporate key aspects of two classic models of direction selectivity.
source: Recent models of direction selectivity in the primary sensing neurons in the fly visual system and mammalian retina incorporate key aspects of two classic models of direction selectivity reviewed by Borst et al., 2020, Murphy-Baum et al., 2021: one relying on multiplicative interactions between excitatory inputs (Hassenstein and Reichardt, 1956) and the other relying on divisive inhibition (Barlow and Levick, 1965).
evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles and classic papers.

claim: The neural substrates underlying inhibition in direction selectivity appear to be well worked out.
source: While the neural substrates underlying inhibition appear to be well worked out, defining the precise sources of excitation and their kinetics has proven to be more difficult.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field.

claim: Defining the precise sources of excitation and their kinetics in direction selectivity has proven to be more difficult.
source: While the neural substrates underlying inhibition appear to be well worked out, defining the precise sources of excitation and their kinetics has proven to be more difficult.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field.

claim: iGluSnFR imaging circumvents many of the uncertainties associated with Ca2+ or electrophysiological measurements from the soma that has typically been applied to assess the properties of input kinetics.
source: This method circumvents many of the uncertainties associated with Ca2+ or electrophysiological measurements from the soma that has typically been applied to assess the properties of input kinetics.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of the iGluSnFR method.

claim: The results demonstrate stark kinetic differences in glutamate input across starburst dendrites, supporting the idea that nonlinear excitatory interactions enhance direction selectivity.
source: Our results demonstrate stark kinetic differences in glutamate input across starburst dendrites, supporting the idea that nonlinear excitatory interactions enhance direction selectivity (Kim et al., 2014; Greene et al., 2016).
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: The input kinetic diversity observed appears to contradict recent large-scale surveys which show BC types of the same response polarity to have similar kinetics.
source: At first pass, the input kinetic diversity across starburst dendrites we observed appears to contradict recent large-scale surveys which show BC types of the same response polarity to have similar kinetics (Franke et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous work.

claim: The discrepancy with previous studies is explained by the choice of precise stimulus parameters.
source: However, this discrepancy is easily explained by the choice of precise stimulus parameters.
evidence: This is an explanation for the apparent contradiction with previous work.

claim: Robust kinetic differences between responses were measured in proximal and distal regions across a range of spot sizes, except for the smallest size that just covered the BC receptive field.
source: Specifically, robust kinetic differences between responses were measured in proximal and distal regions across a range of spot sizes, except for the smallest size that just covered the BC receptive field, which was used by Franke et al., 2017.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experiments.

claim: When larger spots or full-field stimuli are utilized, BC kinetics are found to vary across the inner-plexiform layer.
source: Indeed, when larger spots or full-field stimuli are utilized BC kinetics are found to vary across the inner-plexiform layer (Borghuis et al., 2013; Gaynes et al., 2022; Franke et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Previous studies have shown the functional diversification of BC responses arises mainly from GABAergic and/or glycinergic inhibition.
source: Previous studies have shown the functional diversification of BC responses arises mainly from GABAergic and/or glycinergic inhibition (Franke et al., 2017; Franke and Baden, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: It was surprising to observe clear kinetic differences when all inhibitory pathways were blocked.
source: Thus, it was surprising to observe clear kinetic differences when all inhibitory pathways were blocked.
evidence: This is a statement about the unexpected nature of the finding.

claim: BC kinetics could be influenced by inhibition, but inhibition was not required to generate kinetic differences.
source: This implied that BC kinetics could be influenced by inhibition, but inhibition was not required to generate kinetic differences.
evidence: This is an inference from the pharmacological experiments.

claim: Kinetic differences persist when rod-mediated signals are blocked by CNQX.
source: Additionally, kinetic differences persist when rod-mediated signals are blocked by CNQX suggesting that kinetic differences cannot be attributed solely to changes associated with rod/cone vision, consistent with a previous report (Awatramani and Slaughter, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and citation to Awatramani and Slaughter, 2000.

claim: Input kinetic differences manifest for spot sizes larger than BC dendritic fields, implying that network mechanisms rather than cell-intrinsic factors are involved.
source: The finding that input kinetic differences manifest for spot sizes larger than BC dendritic fields implied that network mechanisms (Figure 4A), rather than cell-intrinsic factors are involved, although these mechanisms are not mutually exclusive (Awatramani and Slaughter, 2000).
evidence: This is an inference from the stimulus size experiments.

claim: Specific types of BCs are known to be coupled to each other as well as to selective amacrine cells including the AII and A8 amacrine cells.
source: Specific types of BCs are known to be coupled to each other as well as to selective amacrine cells including the AII and A8 amacrine cells (Arai et al., 2010; Asari and Meister, 2014; Demb and Singer, 2012; Sigulinsky et al., 2020; Yadav et al., 2019; Zhang and Wu, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Electrical coupling has been implicated in extending BC receptive fields spatially in salamander and fish retinas.
source: Such coupling has been implicated in extending BC receptive fields spatially in salamander and fish retinas (Hare and Owen, 1990; Saito and Kujiraoka, 1988), and in mice, the electrical coupling can non-linearly affect the output of individual BCs (Kuo et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In mice, electrical coupling can non-linearly affect the output of individual BCs.
source: Such coupling has been implicated in extending BC receptive fields spatially in salamander and fish retinas (Hare and Owen, 1990; Saito and Kujiraoka, 1988), and in mice, the electrical coupling can non-linearly affect the output of individual BCs (Kuo et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kuo et al., 2016.

claim: Whether BC7 have stronger coupling patterns compared to BC5 remains to be tested.
source: However, whether BC7 have stronger coupling patterns compared to BC5 remains to be tested.
evidence: This is a statement about a gap in knowledge.

claim: The properties of iGluSnFR signals may depend on a variety of factors including the expression pattern, affinity, and kinetic properties of iGluSnFR.
source: This is not a trivial problem as the properties of iGluSnFR signals may depend on a variety of factors including the expression pattern, affinity, and kinetic properties of iGluSnFR, and in general expected to be vastly different from glutamate receptors that mediate the starburst synaptic responses.
evidence: This is a statement about the complexity of interpreting iGluSnFR signals.

claim: Previous studies have shown iGluSnFR signals reflect local glutamate release from individual BC terminals despite being expressed uniformly along starburst dendrites.
source: Previous studies have shown iGluSnFR signals reflect local glutamate release from individual BC terminals despite being expressed uniformly along starburst dendrites (Borghuis et al., 2013; Franke et al., 2017; Gaynes et al., 2022; Matsumoto et al., 2021; Strauss et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: The deconvolution analysis assumes that the light-evoked responses are made up of a linear superposition of quantal events.
source: This analysis assumes that the light-evoked responses are made up of a linear superposition of quantal events and there is not a significant build-up of glutamate within the synaptic cleft during ongoing activity.
evidence: This is a statement about the assumptions of the analysis method.

claim: The peak instantaneous release rate was estimated to be 5–10 vesicles/s.
source: With these assumptions in mind, we estimated the peak instantaneous release rate to be 5–10 vesicles/s, which is in line with previous in vivo estimates made in zebrafish BC terminals (James et al., 2021; James et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an estimate from the deconvolution analysis supported by comparison to previous work.

claim: The steady-state release rates were estimated to be ~3 vesicles/s at proximal sites and ~1 vesicle/s at distal sites.
source: We also estimated the steady-state release rates to be ~3 vesicles/s at proximal sites and ~1 vesicle/s at distal sites, which is well below the maximum release rate estimated for photoreceptor synapses, which also contain ribbons (Hays et al., 2021; Hays et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an estimate from the deconvolution analysis.

claim: The estimated steady-state release rates are well below the maximum release rate estimated for photoreceptor synapses.
source: We also estimated the steady-state release rates to be ~3 vesicles/s at proximal sites and ~1 vesicle/s at distal sites, which is well below the maximum release rate estimated for photoreceptor synapses, which also contain ribbons (Hays et al., 2021; Hays et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous work on photoreceptor synapses.

claim: The modeling approach contrasts with recent studies in which key parameters were determined by an algorithm that optimizes direction selectivity.
source: Our modeling approach contrasts with recent studies in which key parameters including the vesicle release rates and the specific distribution of BC types along starburst dendrites were determined by an algorithm that optimizes direction selectivity (Ezra-Tsur et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous modeling approaches.

claim: The modeling approach contrasts with phenomenological models such as the linear-non-linear cascade models.
source: It also contrasts with phenomenological models such as the linear-non-linear cascade models, which leave out the biophysical details of the starburst (Kim et al., 2014; Franke et al., 2017; Strauss et al., 2022; Fransen and Borghuis, 2017).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous modeling approaches.

claim: The intrinsic properties of the starburst remain poorly defined.
source: It should be noted, however, that the intrinsic properties of the starburst remain poorly defined and future work is needed to experimentally verify how inputs with distinct kinetics are transformed into dendritic voltage responses.
evidence: This is a statement about limitations and future directions.

claim: The robust direction selectivity that is experimentally observed in starbursts occurs across the range of velocities (100–2000 μm/s).
source: In addition, the robust direction selectivity that is experimentally observed in starbursts occurs across the range of velocities (100–2000 μm/s; Ding et al., 2016; Summers and Feller, 2022), indicating additional mechanisms are involved.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ding et al., 2016 and Summers and Feller, 2022.

claim: Additional mechanisms beyond input kinetics are involved in producing robust direction selectivity across a large range of velocities.
source: In addition, the robust direction selectivity that is experimentally observed in starbursts occurs across the range of velocities (100–2000 μm/s; Ding et al., 2016; Summers and Feller, 2022), indicating additional mechanisms are involved.
evidence: This is an inference from the comparison of model results to experimental observations.

claim: The study emphasizes the role of BC kinetics in driving direction selectivity for slow-moving spots.
source: It is also worth noting while our study emphasizes the role of BC kinetics in driving direction selectivity for slow-moving spots, for other stimuli, such as radial motion, or for stimuli that emerge suddenly, the inhibitory surrounds of BCs may enhance motion sensitivity in more complicated ways (Gaynes et al., 2022; Strauss et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a summary of the main finding of the study.

claim: For other stimuli such as radial motion or stimuli that emerge suddenly, the inhibitory surrounds of BCs may enhance motion sensitivity in more complicated ways.
source: It is also worth noting while our study emphasizes the role of BC kinetics in driving direction selectivity for slow-moving spots, for other stimuli, such as radial motion, or for stimuli that emerge suddenly, the inhibitory surrounds of BCs may enhance motion sensitivity in more complicated ways (Gaynes et al., 2022; Strauss et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gaynes et al., 2022 and Strauss et al., 2022.

claim: Space-time wiring models for direction selectivity have been proposed in diverse systems including the primate retina.
source: Space-time wiring models for direction selectivity have been proposed in diverse systems including the primate retina (Patterson et al., 2022; Kim et al., 2022; Smith et al., 2022), visual cortex (Lien and Scanziani, 2018; De Valois and Cottaris, 1998), as well as the fly optic lobe (Haag et al., 2016; Leong et al., 2016; Behnia et al., 2014; Takemura et al., 2013; but see Takemura et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to work in different systems.

claim: Recent studies have made great strides in identifying the precise anatomical substrates underlying direction selectivity computation in diverse systems.
source: Recent studies have made great strides in identifying the precise anatomical substrates underlying the computation, in all these model systems.
evidence: This is a statement about progress in the field.

claim: Elegant studies assessing presynaptic dynamics provide strong support that anisotropic summation of excitatory signals shapes direction selectivity.
source: Elegant studies assessing presynaptic dynamics, provide strong support that anisotropic summation of excitatory signals shapes direction selectivity (Lien and Scanziani, 2018; Groschner et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lien and Scanziani, 2018 and Groschner et al., 2022.

claim: Proximal and distal starburst dendrites are approximately 5 μm apart in depth.
source: Signals from dendritic regions proximal to the starburst soma were captured in a different optical plane than the more distal dendrites, which are ~5 μm apart (Ding et al., 2016; Greene et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ding et al., 2016 and Greene et al., 2016.

claim: BC7 terminals co-stratify with dendrites of ON starbursts.
source: The intensity profiles of the BC terminals labeled with iGluSnFR (gray), and starburst dendrites labeled with tdTomato (black) across the inner plexiform layer (IPL) show that BC terminals co-stratify with dendrites of ON starbursts (right).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A by the overlapping intensity profiles.

claim: Differences in input kinetics between proximal and distal dendrites provide the first piece of direct evidence supporting the 'space-time' wiring model.
source: Taken together, these results provide the first piece of direct evidence that the kinetics of glutamatergic input varies along starburst dendrites, supporting the 'space-time' wiring model for direction selectivity (Kim et al., 2014; Greene et al., 2016).
evidence: This is the main conclusion from the initial experiments.
